summary: Intake call for Equinox Syndicate to discuss Redwood marketplace listing and hybrid reference architecture. Primary concerns: VPC connectivity, KMS compatibility, quantization tradeoffs for cost, and SOC2/audit evidence. Agreed to run a short perf bench and exchange security artifacts; follow-up POC scoping next week.
transcript:
[00:00] Liam O'Connell: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we're on for about 45 minutes. Quick intros?
[00:08] Rajiv Mehta: Rajiv here, CTO at Equinox Syndicate. We're building a ledger+search product, heavy on embeddings and real-time retrieval.
[00:14] Sofia Patel: Hi, Sofia from Redwood infra, I'll lead the deep tech bits.
[00:18] Ana Torres: Ana, Platform Eng, basically owning our deployment and networking.
[00:22] Marcus Liu: Marcus, security. I'll have a few questions on KMS and audit logs.
[00:26] Liam O'Connell: Great. Agenda I shared: marketplace listing requirements, hybrid refarch patterns (VPC + onprem connector), perf expectations, security checklist, and next steps. Anything else to add?
[00:36] Lena Park: Quick note - product wants the listing to call out latency and cost buckets. Customers care about 95th latency.
[00:42] Liam O'Connell: Perfect, we'll cover SLA-ish metrics.
[00:46] Sofia Patel: To start, can you describe current infra and what you expect from the listing? Are you looking to host on our marketplace image, or want private control plane?
[00:54] Tomás Ruiz: We're leaning hybrid - marketplace for easy onboarding for our customers but also an on-prem connector for enterprise clients with strict residency.
[01:03] Rajiv Mehta: Right. Also we need to know if Redwood supports full VPC peering or if it's just private link-style connectivity. We can't have data egress unless it's encrypted and under our KMS.
[01:11] Sofia Patel: Understood. We support VPC peering and private connectivity in most regions, and for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, and HSM options for onprem). There's a small caveat around the marketplace listing flow - the hosted listing can be configured to use customer-managed KMS during onboarding, but the initial dev/test flow often uses Redwood-managed keys until customer flips.
[01:32] Marcus Liu: That flip is a risk vector for us. Can you share audit logs and attestations for key rotations?
[01:38] Maya Chen: We have an audit package; I'll share a trimmed SOC2 summary and the KMS integration doc after the call. There's also an option for an onprem bundle if you want full key control.
[01:49] Tomás Ruiz: Good. Next: performance. Our use is embeddings + chat-style assistants. Typical sequence lengths vary but inference windows up to 4k tokens are common. What's your recommended model profile?
[02:03] Sofia Patel: For 4k context you probably want a quantized 4-bit LLM for cost, but that depends on latency SLO. If you need sub-200ms token latency at high QPS, Dedicated capacity with GPU pooling is best. For lower cost, hosted with caching and batching can be decent.
[02:21] Ana Torres: Caching details? Our traffic has hot prefixes. We need prefix/prompt KV caching.
[02:26] Sofia Patel: We support prefix KV caching and automatic reuse when prompts match. It reduces token costs and can reduce latency for repeated patterns. We'll need to see your prefix distribution to tune the batch sizes and cache TTL.
[02:38] Rajiv Mehta: Can you run an experiment with our sample traces? We can provide a 24-hour extraction.
[02:43] Liam O'Connell: That's part of the POC plan. Sofia, can you outline the microbench we should run?
[02:47] Sofia Patel: Sure - we'll run 4k context with a mix of 128-token generation and 512-token generation patterns, both GPU (A10/NVIDIA equiv) and CPU quant runs. We'll measure p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. Also test cache hit/miss patterns.
[03:07] Rajiv Mehta: Sounds good. Note: some of our enterprise customers will require air-gapped onprem deployment; is there an onprem package for that?
[03:15] Sofia Patel: Yes - we offer an onprem bundle that includes the Private control plane and a connector image. It requires a Helm chart and a small init job for KV store and metric relay.
[03:25] Tomás Ruiz: Helm chart—will you provide an example and CRDs?
[03:28] Sofia Patel: Yes, we'll share an example Helm package tailored for marketplace listing. It includes CRDs for model versions and rollout policies.
[03:36] Marcus Liu: Back to security: how are logs handled? We need customer-viewable audit trails and ability to forward to Splunk/ELK or Cloud Logging.
[03:44] Maya Chen: You can forward audit logs via syslog or push to cloud logging endpoints. For Marketplace listings we surface audit logs via the console and offer log streaming integration as an add-on.
[03:54] Marcus Liu: And data retention policies? We have regulatory constraints for 7-year retention for some records.
[04:00] Maya Chen: That is doable via the retention config in Redwood Console; we'll map retention buckets to your policy. For Private/onprem, you fully control retention.
[04:08] Lena Park: On the listing, our product team wants the model catalog entries to have cost bands. Do you provide cost estimation?
[04:14] Liam O'Connell: We provide per-token cost estimates and also estimated monthly costs by usage profile. We'll share a pricing anchor doc.
[04:21] Rajiv Mehta: Any known limitations with quantized models and long-context? We saw hallucination increase in some 4-bit runs.
[04:29] Sofia Patel: Right, quantization can impact output quality at extremes. Our Optimize toolkit suggests quant profiles per workload; you'll want to tie quality regressions to eval prompt sets. We can help run those evals.
[04:44] Ana Torres: Network egress and latency - if we do marketplace listing but want traffic routed from our VPC, how is routing controlled?
[04:51] Sofia Patel: For marketplace you can configure smart routing: route-by-policy either to Redwood hosted nodes or to your Dedicated pool. We'll work with NetOps to set up route tables and peering.
[05:01] Tomás Ruiz: Any special ports or firewall rules needed?
[05:04] Sofia Patel: Mainly gRPC/HTTPS outbound to Redwood endpoints; exact CIDR ranges we'll provide. There's also a connector heartbeat on 443.
[05:11] Rajiv Mehta: Can the connector be restricted to internal IPs only?
[05:14] Sofia Patel: Yes, the connector can be deployed in your private subnet and only allow internal traffic.
[05:18] Liam O'Connell: Let's talk deliverables. We'll send two artifacts: the marketplace listing checklist and the onprem Helm example. Equinox will send sample traces and security artifacts.
[05:27] Lena Park: Timeline: product wants a public listing within Q2 if POC goes well.
[05:32] Liam O'Connell: Q2 is ambitious but possible. POC needs to start next week ideally.
[05:36] Rajiv Mehta: On pricing - we need a ballpark model for marketplace vs dedicated so our finance can model numbers.
[05:42] Liam O'Connell: We'll provide pricing anchors and a committed-capacity vs pay-as-you-go comparison.
[05:47] Marcus Liu: Quick compliance question - do you support SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning for team access in the marketplace?
[05:54] Maya Chen: Yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and SCIM for user provisioning on enterprise tiers.
[06:00] Tomás Ruiz: If we choose an onprem bundle, what's the upgrade path?
[06:04] Sofia Patel: We provide a versioned Helm chart with a control plane upgrade path, release notes, and a runbook for DB migrations. For air-gapped installs there's a tarball release process.
[06:14] Rajiv Mehta: Good. Any blockers right now?
[06:16] Marcus Liu: Need to review the KMS attestation and the audit log sample. Also want to validate the connector's network model.
[06:25] Sofia Patel: We'll produce a short network diagram and sample config for the connector.
[06:29] Liam O'Connell: Okay, let's capture next steps. We'll run the perf microbench, share the security pack, and schedule the POC scoping call.
[06:37] Rajiv Mehta: One more ask - can you include a short section in the listing about fallback policies if Dedicated capacity is saturated? We want predictable degradation modes.
[06:46] Sofia Patel: Absolutely - Redwood supports model fallbacks and region fallback as a policy. We'll include examples and expected latency impact.
[06:53] Lena Park: Thanks, that helps product planning.
[06:56] Liam O'Connell: Any final questions?
[07:00] Tomás Ruiz: No, thanks.
[07:02] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with the SOC2 summary and listing checklist.
[07:06] Rajiv Mehta: Thanks, everyone.
[07:08] Liam O'Connell: Great, we'll send notes and action items. End call.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings; speaker labels may be slightly off in automated export. Attached references: marketplace-checklist.xlsx (link shared via email), onprem-helm-example.tgz (shared to dropbox), security-pack.pdf (Redwood link).
